err.emptyPattern: An empty pattern in the item {item}
err.patternBadPort: The pattern {pattern}: the port {port} is not a number
err.patternEmptyPart: The pattern {pattern} in the item {item}: an empty login or host
plugin.ssh.description: An ssh agent: the vault’s keys sign without ever reaching the disk
plugin.ssh.title: SSH
routes.empty.body: Pick an SSH key and list its hosts, comma separated — for example *.example.net, gitlab.example.com. From then on ssh gets exactly that key and nothing else.
routes.empty.title: No host is bound to a key yet
routes.title: Host → key
settings.sshAgentHint: A disabled agent behaves as an absent one: ssh falls back to key files.
settings.sshAskHint: Confirmation is asked via Touch ID.
settings.sshConfigHint: At the end of the file, and nowhere else: ssh reads it top to bottom, and %h in Match exec is whatever is known by that line. Above the Host blocks that is the alias you typed ("vps"), not the host name, and no route is found. The path is absolute on purpose: Match exec runs through /bin/sh, where PATH differs.
settings.sshSocketHint: One socket with every key — for IDEs and git clients that ignore ssh_config. ssh will try keys one by one, as with a regular agent.
settings.sshSocketPathHint: Add the line to ~/.zshrc or the app's settings. The socket lives while the vault is unlocked.
sshkey.importHint: A new Ed25519 key is made for you. To use your own, copy its private key (OpenSSH or RSA in PEM) and press “Import from clipboard”: it is checked at once.
sshkey.passphraseHint: Used once to open the key; it is not stored.
sshkey.privateStored: The private key stays in the vault and is never shown here: the agent signs with it without it reaching the disk.
sshkey.regenerateHint: A new pair replaces this one on save. Servers that have the old public key in authorized_keys will stop letting it in until the new one is put there.
sshkey.replaceHint: Copy a private key you already have and import it from the clipboard; it is checked first. The old key stops working wherever only it was trusted.
sshkey.replacingWarn: On save the current key is replaced for good: servers that trust only the old public key will stop letting you in.
err.sshKnownHostsUnreadable: The host keys file {path} will not read, so no host can be checked against it
err.sshKnownHostsUnwritable: The host key could not be saved to {path}
err.sshHostKeyNotPinned: The key {host} presented is not the one pinned in the item (kw-hostkey). It presented {fingerprint}. Nothing was signed.
err.sshHostKeyChanged: The host key of {host}:{port} has changed. It now presents {fingerprint}. This is what an attack in the middle looks like, so nothing was signed. If the server was really reinstalled, forget the old key and connect again.
err.sshHostKeyDeclined: The key of {host} was not trusted ({fingerprint}); the connection was dropped
err.sshNoPublicKey: The key “{key}” has no public half to offer
err.sshKeyRejected: {host} did not accept the key “{key}” for {user}. Check that its public half is in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of that user.
err.sshNothingToTrust: There is no host key waiting for an answer
err.sshLinkGone: The terminal lost its sealed link; open the session again
err.sshNoSession: This terminal is not attached to a session
err.sshTooManySessions: Already {max} sessions are open; close one first
err.sshBadHost: That is not a host name
err.sshNoKeyForHost: No key is bound to {host}. Bind a key to it under Keys, or pick a key when connecting.
err.sshKeyGone: The key is no longer in the vault
err.sshTerminalCertUnsupported: The key “{key}” signs in with a certificate (kw-cert); the terminal does not do certificates yet
err.sshLoginRequired: Which login on {host}? Type it, or write it into the route as login@{host}
err.sshTerminalBroken: The terminal broke inside; open the session again
term.noHosts: Hosts of your keys appear here. Bind a key to hosts in Keys, or connect by hand.
term.keyByRoute: The one the routes give the host
term.connectHint: The private key never leaves the vault: keyward signs the login and asks you to confirm it.
term.authenticatingHint: keyward signs in to {where} with the key “{key}” once you confirm.
term.verify.title: First connection to {host}
term.verify.body: Nobody has vouched for this server’s key yet. Compare the fingerprint with the one its administrator gives you; once trusted, it is remembered and checked every time.
term.verify.others: Keys of another kind are already known for this host. The server may have been reinstalled — or someone may be pretending to be it.
term.state.verify: Waiting for your answer about the host key
term.empty.title: No SSH keys yet
term.empty.body: Add an SSH key to the vault and bind it to its hosts: its health shows here, and a shell is one click away.
term.health.title: Key health
term.health.good: Hosts that let the key in: {n} of {total}
term.health.explain: Each key is offered to the hosts it is bound to, without signing: the server only says whether it would let the key in. No confirmation is asked and the private key is not touched.
term.health.reachableHint: Set a login for this key under Hosts to check the key itself
term.health.hostUnknownHint: Connect once and trust the host key to check this key
term.health.unboundHint: This key is bound to no host. Press Bind and list its hosts to check it.
term.health.wildcardHint: Its routes are patterns such as *.example.com. A host you connect to through them is checked from then on.
term.health.changedHint: The host key changed: nothing is signed for this host until the key is sorted out
settings.sshHealthHint: Offers each key to its hosts without signing and shows who still lets it in.
routes.loginHint: What the terminal and the health checks log in as, where a host above names no login@ and :port. It is filled in by itself after the first successful sign-in.
err.sshBadPortField: The key “{key}” has a port that is not a number: {port}
err.sshNotSsh: {host} answered, but not as an ssh server
err.sshConfigUnreadable: ~/.ssh/config at {path} will not read, so it is not trusted for anything
err.sshProxyJumpUnsupported: {host} is reached through {jump} (ProxyJump in ~/.ssh/config); the terminal does not go through jump hosts yet
err.sshTimedOutReach: {host} did not complete the connection within {seconds} s
err.sshTimedOutLogin: {host} did not answer the sign-in within {seconds} s
err.sshTimedOutShell: {host} let you in but did not open a shell within {seconds} s
term.forgotten: The old key is forgotten; connect again and check the new one.
term.notOurs: The old key is in ~/.ssh/known_hosts; keyward does not edit that file — remove the line there if the server was really reinstalled.
ssh.verify: The first connection to {host}: compare the {algorithm} key's fingerprint with what the server shows
ssh.verifyOthers: {host} is known by keys of another kind: the server may have changed its key. Compare the {algorithm} fingerprint
